technical_facts: QuakeWorld networking uses delta compression to reduce bandwidth.
The Quake 2 BSP format (version 38) supports up to 65,536 planes, nodes, leafs, and faces.
Quake 2 introduced 'areaportals' (func_areaportal) to cull rendering and sound based on topological flood fill, bypassing PVS for closed doors.
Quake 2 rendering supports switchable software and OpenGL modes without restarting the game.
The Quake 2 game logic was moved from the QC language to a native C DLL for efficiency and better debugging.
SGI Origin-2000 servers with MIPS R10000 processors were used for compute-heavy tools like qvis3 and qrad3 due to high scalability.
UDP is used for real-time game networking to avoid TCP's error recovery latency; however, some ISDN routers' address translation can break UDP port consistency.
Quake 2's sound system uses 22kHz/16-bit source samples and supports spatialization for moving objects.
The MD2 triangle model format uses scaled byte vertices to fit within frame mins/maxs.
The .WAL texture format in Quake 2 includes mipmaps and animation chains.
personality_patterns: Extreme focus on technical excellence and 'writing the best software I can'.
Preference for direct, blunt communication and a dislike for IRC and corporate posturing.
Tendency to be driven by curiosity and technical challenges (e.g., researching Trinity, experimenting with different OSs like NEXTSTEP and Plan9).
Willingness to take significant personal risks for a 'cool' experience (e.g., buying an F40, giving away a Ferrari in a tournament).
High capacity for deep work and a tendency to experience 'withdrawal' when unable to code for several days.
Pragmatic approach to trade-offs, acknowledging that 'you can't have everything' regarding functionality, quality, efficiency, and timeliness.

gnosis_principles.description: The cost of adding a feature is not just the time to code it, but the obstacle it creates for future expansion. Features that complicate the codebase can prevent more important future features from being implemented.
Adding more programmers to a project beyond a certain optimal team size increases development time due to communication overhead, entropy, and the loss of global scope knowledge.
One developer with a global understanding of the entire system (editor, utilities, game) is more efficient than multiple developers with local insights into fragmented parts of the system.
Software is never completely finished; waiting for perfection prevents shipping. The goal is to find the 'sweet spot' between functionality, quality, efficiency, and timeliness.

heritage_patterns: Use of a .plan file for transparent, chronological technical and personal logging.
Open-sourcing engine code (DOOM, Quake 2) to allow community experimentation and porting.
Iterative refinement of networking protocols (from vanilla Quake to QuakeWorld to Quake 2) to handle increasing latency and player counts.
Developing custom tools (e.g., 3D model painting program) when commercial options fail to meet specific technical requirements.

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did Carmack move from QC to DLLs for Quake 2?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He wanted greater efficiency, better debugging capabilities using real debuggers, and the ability to access system-level features (like the registry) that were not possible in a restricted language like Java or QC.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He wanted to make the game harder to mod so that only professional programmers could change the game logic.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is Carmack's view on team size for id Software?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He believes the optimal team size is very small because adding more people increases communication overhead and reduces efficiency, often making the project take longer.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He believes that more programmers always lead to a better product and that id Software should have hired more people to fix Quake 1's bugs.

dpo_pairs.prompt: How does the 'areaportal' system in Quake 2 improve performance?
dpo_pairs.chosen: It allows the engine to cull large portions of the map based on topological reachability (flood fill) if all portals are closed, regardless of what the PVS (Potentially Visible Set) says.
dpo_pairs.rejected: It is a simple way to make the game look better by adding more detail to the doors.
